title: Density-aware focus ring and locale-sensitive name truncation sweep for compact cost tiles
creator: Maya Chen
description: Sweep to finalize keyboard and screenreader UX for compact cost metric tiles when rendered at high density and in non-Latin locales. Goals: 1) ensure focus treatments remain visually distinct without increasing perceived noise when cards are tiled tightly; 2) prevent awkward mid-grapheme truncation for CJK and combined-script names; 3) stabilize accessible label composition so AT reads concise, actionable text; 4) validate color token deltas across theme modes (light/dark/high-contrast) and across localized number formats.
acceptance_criteria: Keyboard focus visible and meets 4.1.2 contrast ratio for all theme modes at 72px and 48px tile densities
Tile titles truncate on grapheme cluster boundaries (no mid-character truncation for CJK, emoji, diacritics)
Screen reader reads: "<tile title> — <primary metric> — <unit>" and does not announce redundant visual hints
No layout shift > 3px when focus ring appears and when locale changes numeric separators
QA matrix: tested Chrome/Edge/Safari on Mac/Windows, and Chrome/Android; documented results
decisions: Adopt 2px outer focus ring with 1px inner offset for high-density mode; reduces perceived outline thickness while meeting contrast targets
Implement grapheme-aware truncation using Intl.Segmenter where available, fallback to unicode-segmentation library server-side for older browsers
Compose aria-label server-side to avoid reliance on DOM concatenation; use localized unit strings from i18n catalog
Use token contrast delta mapping: +12% luminance for focus ring in dark theme and +18% in high-contrast mode (design tokens updated)
next_steps: ENG: ship grapheme-aware truncation polyfill in shared ui/text-utils (ENG-4278)
Design: update token tokens/figma styles and export new CSS variables (complete)
PM: schedule cross-team QA window 2025-03-03 to 2025-03-04
Accessibility: run NVDA and VoiceOver pass and add results to ticket comments
